findings.problem: loadGRPCRoute is a near line-for-line copy of loadHTTPRoute (httproute.go:29). The parentRef/listener matching, the Accepted reason cascade, the AttachedRoutes and attachedRoutes bookkeeping, the ResolvedRefs selection, the servedRules merge and the status recording are all repeated. Only the route kind, the per-listener configuration loader and the Record*Status call differ. Any future fix to attachment semantics has to be made twice.
findings.fix: Extract a shared helper, e.g. `p.attachHTTPLikeRoute(ctx, gateways, obj metav1.Object, kind string, hostnames []gatev1.Hostname, parentRefs []gatev1.ParentReference, loadConf func(listener gatewayListener, gwName, gwNs string, hostnames []gatev1.Hostname) ([]routeRouter, metav1.Condition), record func(gatev1.RouteParentStatus), ...)`. Make loadHTTPRoute and loadGRPCRoute thin wrappers that pass kindHTTPRoute/kindGRPCRoute, their configuration loader and statusReport.RecordHTTPRouteStatus/RecordGRPCRouteStatus.

findings.problem: grpcRouteRouter, httpRouteRouter (httproute.go:126) and tlsRouteRouter (tlsroute.go:134) are three identical {Name string; Conf *dynamic.Configuration} types.
findings.fix: Replace them with one package-level `type routeRouter struct { Name string; Conf *dynamic.Configuration }` in kubernetes.go, and use it in all three loaders.

findings.problem: The BackendTLSPolicy handling is copied three times: sorting, targetRef/sectionName filtering, ancestor status building, conflict conditions, Accepted/ResolvedRefs conditions and the error route condition. The copies are in loadGRPCServers, loadHTTPServers (httproute.go:579) and loadTLSServers (tlsroute.go:361). Each copy also re-applies the Gateway backend client certificate. The copies have already drifted: the HTTP copy says 'wen wrong' in a comment.
findings.fix: Extract `p.resolveBackendTLSPolicy(gatewayName, gatewayNamespace, namespace string, routeGeneration int64, backendRef gatev1.BackendObjectReference, svcPort corev1.ServicePort, listener gatewayListener, load func(*gatev1.BackendTLSPolicy) (T, metav1.Condition), statusReport) (T, *metav1.Condition)`. A generic T, or a returned *gatev1.BackendTLSPolicy that callers convert, would also work. Call it from the three loadXServers functions.

findings.problem: loadTCPServersTransport duplicates loadServersTransport (httproute.go:708). The SAN mapping, the WellKnownCACertificates handling and the ConfigMap/Secret ca.crt resolution with all its conditions are the same. Only the target struct differs (TCPServersTransport.TLS vs ServersTransport).
findings.fix: Extract `p.resolveBackendTLSValidation(namespace string, policy *gatev1.BackendTLSPolicy) (serverName string, insecureSkipVerify bool, sans []tls.SAN, rootCAs []types.FileOrContent, cond metav1.Condition, ok bool)`. Keep the two thin functions only to fill dynamic.ServersTransport and dynamic.TLSClientConfig from its result.

findings.problem: The deny-unknown-host router and service are written inside the `for _, route := range routes` loop. They are rewritten on every iteration, and the code reads as if they were per-route state.
findings.fix: Move the `if len(conf.TCP.Routers) > 0 { ... }` block after the routes loop so it runs once.

findings.problem: UpdateHTTPRouteStatus (527), UpdateGRPCRouteStatus, UpdateTCPRouteStatus and UpdateTLSRouteStatus have the same body; only the lister/client accessors and the status type differ. The copies have drifted: the GRPC error message uses `%q` with route.Name only, while the others use namespace/name.
findings.fix: Extract `updateRouteParentStatus(ctx, kind string, route ktypes.NamespacedName, gateways []gatewayWithListeners, desired []gatev1.RouteParentStatus, get func() ([]gatev1.RouteParentStatus, error), update func(parents []gatev1.RouteParentStatus) error) error`, which holds the watched-namespace check, RetryOnConflict, merge, equality check and error wrapping. Have each Update*RouteStatus pass closures. This also unifies the error message to `%s/%s`.

findings.problem: routeParentStatusesEqual duplicates policyAncestorStatusesEqual, a two-way ContainsFunc set comparison. listenerEntryStatusesEqual (976) duplicates listenersStatusEqual for a field-for-field mirror type.
findings.fix: Add a generic `unorderedEqualFunc[T any](a, b []T, eq func(T, T) bool) bool` and use it in both *StatusesEqual functions. Define listenersStatusEqual by converting to ListenerEntryStatus, or make one generic helper over a shared comparator, so the per-listener comparison exists once.

findings.problem: withoutForeignConditions and mergeGatewayStatus (860) each repeat the 'owned condition' predicates `slices.Contains(gatewayConditionTypes, c.Type)` and `slices.Contains(listenerConditionTypes, c.Type)`. Ownership is therefore decided in four places.
findings.fix: Add `isOwnedGatewayCondition(c metav1.Condition) bool` and `isOwnedListenerCondition(c metav1.Condition) bool` next to the vars, and use them in both functions.

findings.problem: The parentRef→listenerOwner defaulting (Kind defaults to Gateway, Namespace defaults to the route namespace) is duplicated here and in matchingGatewayListenersForParentRef (kubernetes.go:1880).
findings.fix: Add `func parentRefOwner(routeNamespace string, ref gatev1.ParentReference) listenerOwner` in kubernetes.go and use it in both places.

findings.problem: The check that a listener is declared by a given ListenerSet owner (`listener.ListenerSet != nil && listener.ListenerSet.Namespace == owner.Namespace && listener.ListenerSet.Name == owner.Name`) is repeated in matchingGatewayListenersForParentRef and gatewayForOwner (1924).
findings.fix: Add a method `func (o listenerOwner) declares(l gatewayListener) bool` that handles both the Gateway and ListenerSet kinds, and use it in both functions.

findings.problem: The gateways comparator and the listenerSets comparator (465) re-implement compareRoutes inline. compareRoutes already takes metav1.Object.
findings.fix: Rename compareRoutes to compareObjects (creation timestamp, then namespace, then name). Use `slices.SortStableFunc(gateways, func(a, b *gatev1.Gateway) int { return compareObjects(a, b) })` and the same for listenerSets.

findings.problem: loadHTTPBackendRef uses the literal "TraefikService" and dereferences *backendRef.Kind and *backendRef.Group without nil checks. kindTraefikService and isTraefikService already exist. The function is reached whenever group != core or kind != Service, so a nil Group combined with a non-Service Kind panics.
findings.fix: Replace the condition with `isTraefikService(backendRef.BackendRef) && strings.Contains(...)`. Use the group/kind already defaulted by loadService, by passing them in as parameters, instead of dereferencing the pointers. Apply the same change to the copy in tcproute.go:352.

findings.problem: The test case structs declare fields that no test reads: `expectErr` here, and `expectedError` in Test_buildMatchRule (line 79).
findings.fix: Remove the unused expectErr and expectedError fields.

kept.problem: loadHTTPBackendRef uses the literal "TraefikService" and dereferences *backendRef.Kind and *backendRef.Group without nil checks. kindTraefikService and isTraefikService already exist. The function is reached whenever group != core or kind != Service, so a nil Group combined with a non-Service Kind panics.
kept.fix: Replace the condition with `isTraefikService(backendRef.BackendRef) && strings.Contains(...)`. Use the group/kind already defaulted by loadService, by passing them in as parameters, instead of dereferencing the pointers. Apply the same change to the copy in tcproute.go:352.
kept.why: loadService defaults Kind to Service, then calls loadHTTPBackendRef when group != core or kind != Service. A backendRef with a non-core Group and no Kind therefore reaches `*backendRef.Kind` (httproute.go:424) and panics on a nil pointer. loadTCPBackendRef (tcproute.go:352) has the same nil dereference. Both also use the literal "TraefikService" even though kindTraefikService and isTraefikService already exist.
